answer: One defense is latency triangulation. Validators spread like posts along a wharf ping each agent with random nonces at unpredictable moments, and round-trip times pin down where its hardware sits. Fifty fake agents on one rack return near-identical timings, so they collapse into a single reward share. Faking it means renting real machines in distant cities, a basalt-hard cost paid per head, so a sybil farm's profit never reaches its summit.
